title: Operational capacity solver and license heuristics
content:
Executive summary:
A compact spreadsheet-style playbook that teams can use to compare on-prem vs VPC private deployments with explicit license + support bundle tradeoffs. Focus is on marginal unit cost per 1k QPS, payback horizon for hardware amortization, and an ops-effort index that converts FTEs into an equivalent monthly cost. This is intended for solutions engineering and pricing discussions — not final legal quotes.

Key assumptions (editable input cells):
- Discount rate (annual): 10%
- Hardware refresh cycle: 36 months (default)
- Rack-level overhead (power + datacenter): 18% of hardware capex annually
- Average utilization target: 45% (90th percentile burst handled by burst pool)
- Support SLA uplift (bronze/silver/gold): 5% / 10% / 20% of license fee monthly respectively
- License model baseline: per-GPU-month on dedicated pool OR committed QPS seat for VPC
- Ops-effort index: 0.12 FTE per 100k sustained QPS for on-prem baseline

Input table (CSV style, editable):
Scenario,deployment_type,upfront_capex_usd,monthly_infra_opex_usd,license_monthly_usd,support_percent,committed_qps,amortize_months,ops_ftes
Base-onprem,OnPrem,850000,12000,0,0,200000,36,1.0
Base-vpc,VPC,0,42000,32000,0.10,200000,0,0.2
Hybrid-committed,Hybrid,220000,15000,12000,0.08,300000,36,0.5
Small-edge,OnPrem,160000,6000,0,0,40000,36,0.2

Derived formulas (notes for spreadsheet implementation):
- monthly_capex_amort = upfront_capex_usd / amortize_months
- monthly_support_usd = license_monthly_usd * support_percent
- ops_cost_usd = ops_ftes * (fte_loaded_salary_monthly)  # fte_loaded_salary_monthly is an input cell e.g. $14,000
- monthly_total_cost = monthly_infra_opex_usd + monthly_capex_amort + license_monthly_usd + monthly_support_usd + ops_cost_usd
- cost_per_1k_qps = (monthly_total_cost / committed_qps) * 1000
- payback_months = upfront_capex_usd / (vpc_delta_monthly_savings)  # where vpc_delta_monthly_savings = vpc_equivalent_monthly_total - onprem_monthly_total

Sample sensitivity outputs (textual):
- If utilization moves from 45% -> 60% (all else equal) on OnPrem, cost_per_1k_qps drops ~18% because amortization is spread over more effective tokens/QPS.
- Increasing support SLA from Silver (10%) -> Gold (20%) adds ~9% to total monthly outlay for license-dominant scenarios.
- Shortening refresh cycle to 24 months increases monthly amortization by 50%, increasing cost_per_1k_qps materially for hardware-heavy configurations.

Ops-effort indexing and negotiation levers:
- Convert FTEs into a monthly ops_cost_usd using a loaded rate cell; for sales conversations include a conservative 20% hiring buffer.
- For customers with heavy security/compliance needs (air-gapped), apply a 12-18% premium to ops_effort and a one-time integration support fee.
- Licensing levers to propose: committed-qps discounts at 6/12/24 month terms, burst credits (pay-per-burst), and ticket-response SLAs that can be upsold.

NPV-style break-even sketch (high level):
- Compute cashflow stream for OnPrem: -upfront_capex in month 0, +monthly_total_cost negative each month. For VPC: 0 upfront, monthly_vpc_total_cost negative each month. Discount each cashflow at the discount rate. Compute NPV(onprem) vs NPV(vpc) across horizon (36 months default).
- Interpret: NPV(onprem) < NPV(vpc) implies on-prem is cheaper across horizon. Payback month is first month cumulative delta > upfront_capex.

Negotiation playbook (for SEs):
- If customer expects > 36 months of stable high utilization (>60%), lead with on-prem TCO but structure a hybrid pilot (6–12 months) with committed QPS and optional buyout.
- If usage is spiky and <45% sustained, prefer VPC or hybrid with burst credits; sell support SLAs and faster cloud routing for tail latency guarantees.
- For enterprise procurement: present three bundles (Starter, Sustained, Mission-critical) with clearly separated items: license, support SLA, optional dedicated network (VPC peering), and professional services (onboarding + security hardening).

Risks and mitigations:
- Forecast risk: overestimating utilization -> on-prem becomes expensive. Mitigate by including covenant-based buyout options.
- Ops churn: high FTE turnover increases hidden costs. Mitigate by offering managed ops addon for first 12 months at discounted rate.
- Hardware supply / lead time: model a 4–12 week contingency line and include temporary cloud bursting credits in contract.

Practical next steps (owner + quick checklist):
- SEs: copy this sheet into a customer-specific workbook and fill inputs (owner: Ben Martin).
- Pricing: validate license_monthly_usd against current rate card and compute tiered discounts (owner: Aisha Kapoor).
- Legal: draft standard buyout clause for committed pool conversion to license credit (owner: Rajesh Patel).
- Engineering: confirm typical ops_ftes for the given architecture (owner: Carmen Liu).

Appendix: example quick comparison (rounded numbers):
CSV: Scenario,monthly_total_usd,cost_per_1k_qps_usd,payback_months,hypothesis
Base-onprem,42500,212.5,16,"High upfront, cheaper at >36 months if utilization holds"
Base-vpc,76000,380.0,NA,"No upfront, higher steady-state, good for spiky loads"
Hybrid-committed,42000,140.0,7,"Moderate upfront, best when committed QPS > base and desire for isolation"

Notes to SEs (fragile items to flag in slides):
- Calls out sensitivity to FTE loaded rates and refresh cycle: make sure customer agrees on assumptions in writing.
- Show both 24- and 36-month refresh scenarios in every pitch.
- Include a slide that converts cost_per_1k_qps into cost per 1M tokens for LLM evaluation workloads to make it relatable to product PMs.

Raw CSV export block to drop into a sheet (repeatable):
